A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GAL‐LI in molly is sexually dimorphic, but not sexually segregated, in the brainstem, and that GAL‐LI is sexually dimorphic in the spinal cord but is not sexually segregated.

the distribution of GAL‐LI is sexually dimorphic in the molly and that GAL‐LI neurons are located in the dorsal root, dorsal and ventral motor, and interneuronal columns of the spinal cord, and that GAL‐IL neurons in the dorsal motor column are sexually dimorphic.

the GAL‐LI in molly spinal cord is derived from a number of GAL‐LI neurons of origin in both sexes, including the dorsal root ganglion (DRG), the dorsal horn and, to a limited degree, the ventral horn.

the GAL‐LI system of the molly brainstem and spinal is not sexually dimorphic, but that it is sexually dimorphic at the level of the dorsal root ganglion.
